clue.text: Leader of jazz quartet originally engaged for dance

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so take the start of jazz

parts.note: a quartet is four, and four in Roman numerals is IV

indicators.note: originally points to the very first letter of the word engaged

explanation.surface: A jazz bandleader's quartet was first hired to play for a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Jive is a lively swing-era style of dancing, so it names a dance.

clue.text: Fool's device for raising heavy weights on a ship

parts.note: a jack lifts heavy loads such as a car
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Some idiot's contraption for hoisting heavy loads aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just joins JACK to A plus SS; the 's of 'Fool's' stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackass is a stupid person, from the male donkey.

clue.text: Malice shown by highly honoured cleric?

parts.note: Ven. is short for Venerable, the title of an archdeacon
OM is the Order of Merit, a very high British honour

explanation.surface: Spite is displayed by a decorated churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: Venom is bitter spite or hostility, malice in speech or manner.

clue.text: Endless hunting expedition seen in the distance

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its first and last letters, here the synonym for the expedition

parts.note: a safari is a hunting expedition, especially in Africa

explanation.surface: A hunting trip that never ends is glimpsed far off on the horizon.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar is an adverb meaning at a great distance, far away.

clue.text: Reportedly, Spanish king's shot in the arm

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is heard, so the word is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: Philip was the name of several kings of Spain, such as Philip II

explanation.surface: Rumour has it a monarch of Spain was shot in the arm.
explanation.definitionFit: A fillip is a stimulus or boost, figuratively a shot in the arm.

clue.text: Little money deposited in bank of late

indicators.note: deposited in means one piece is placed inside the other, as cash into an account

parts.note: to bank on something is to rely on it
a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: Not long ago some loose change was paid into the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks like a noun for money but is the verb, as in 'bank on', giving RELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Recently means lately, of late.

clue.text: Greek character with gun crossing range

indicators.note: crossing means one piece goes across, spanning the other, so the gun word is set around the letter

parts.note: gat is old gangster slang for a gun
mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek man with a gun strides across a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamut is the full range or scope of something, originally the whole musical scale.

clue.text: Attacked a Staffordshire town no longer in existence

parts.note: to go for someone is to attack them, so gone for means attacked
Burton upon Trent is a brewing town in Staffordshire, a Midlands county of England

explanation.surface: A Midlands town was assaulted and has now vanished from the map.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is RAF slang from the Second World War for an airman lost or killed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means lost, dead or destroyed, simply vanished.

clue.text: Kentish town supplying servants to Northumberland?

parts.note: maids are household servants
taken as written
Northumberland is in north-east England, abbreviated NE

explanation.surface: A town in Kent sends domestic staff up to the far north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Maidstone is the county town of Kent, in south-east England.

clue.text: A bar for swinging performers

parts.note: reads like a nightclub for jazz musicians or partner-swapping guests, but is a circus bar on ropes for acrobats

explanation.definitionFit: A trapeze is a horizontal bar hung on ropes on which acrobats swing.

clue.text: Take a bold approach, and risk getting stung

definitions.meaning: to tackle a difficulty head-on and firmly
literally to seize a stinging weed with the hand

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means tackle a problem boldly; literally, gripping a stinging plant firmly risks a sting.

clue.text: Under which we're in order to identify spymaster

definitions.meaning: being under it means things are kept orderly and in check
in John le Carré's spy novels the head of British intelligence is known by this codename

explanation.definitionFit: Being in control keeps order; le Carré's spy chief is called Control, so the word doubles as a codename.

clue.text: Girl with drink container in wine shop

parts.note: a can holds a drink such as beer or soda
Tina is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl with a can of drink sits in a wine bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantina is a Spanish or Latin American bar or wine shop.

clue.text: Acknowledgment of entry

definitions.meaning: a confession or acceptance that something is true
the right or act of entering, as with a ticket

explanation.definitionFit: Admission means both owning up to something and being let in to a place.

clue.text: German force penetrating enemy trench

indicators.note: penetrating means one piece pushes into the middle of the other, here the force into the enemy

parts.note: a foe is an enemy
the SS was the Nazi German paramilitary force

explanation.surface: German troops break through into an enemy trench.
explanation.definitionFit: A fosse is a ditch or moat dug as a defence, a kind of trench.

clue.text: Improperly hustle crime investigator

indicators.note: improperly means the letters of the following word are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A detective is accused of jostling someone in an improper way.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleuth is a detective, someone who investigates crimes.

clue.text: Never having gained experience in the plant

definitions.meaning: read as ..., always green, meaning permanently inexperienced
a tree or shrub that keeps its leaves all year

explanation.definitionFit: Green means inexperienced, so ever green is always naive; an evergreen is a plant keeping its foliage year-round.

clue.text: Ring of light in Cockney's untidy room, say?

indicators.note: say tells us to judge the words by how they are spoken out loud

parts.note: a glory hole is a cluttered storage room, and a Cockney drops the H to make it glory 'ole

explanation.surface: A halo seems to hover in a Londoner's messy junk room.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney (an East Londoner) drops initial H, so 'glory hole', a room where junk is dumped, comes out as 'glory 'ole'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gloriole is a halo or aureole, a ring of light round a holy figure's head.

clue.text: List of cargo employee provided is from France

parts.note: a man is a worker, as in a hired man
provided means if, as in on condition that
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A ship's freight list shows that a worker comes from France.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifest is a document listing a ship's cargo or passengers.

clue.text: Vassal's story accepted by European right away

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story

indicators.note: right away means the letter R, short for right, is taken out of the following word

parts.note: a German is a European
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A vassal's tale is swiftly believed by a European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'immediately' but means remove R (right) from GERMAN, leaving GEMAN; 'accepted by' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A liegeman was a feudal vassal sworn to serve his lord.

clue.text: Smoothly move over, thus identifying sort of rock

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the letters of the motion word run backwards

parts.note: to sail is to move smoothly
sic is Latin for thus

explanation.surface: A geologist glides across, naming a type of stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Liassic describes the Lias, a series of early Jurassic rock strata.

clue.text: Wretched article replacing front of another

indicators.note: replacing the front means the opening letters of the word are swapped out for the new piece

parts.note: another word for the vassal in the clue before, a subject being someone ruled by a monarch
the opening two letters of the synonym that are removed
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A miserable news item supplants the lead of another story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' points back to 18 across: another word for vassal is SUBJECT, and the article A replaces its front, SU.
explanation.definitionFit: Abject describes a miserable, hopeless condition, a synonym of wretched.

clue.text: Ancient token girl's taken without hesitation

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the girl's name goes around the pause

parts.note: Tessa is a girl's name
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A girl grabs an old coin without pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but is used in its old sense of outside, so the girl's name surrounds the pause; 'taken' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera was a small tile or tablet used in antiquity as a token or ticket.

clue.text: Small marks in glasses, say

indicators.note: say means as spoken out loud, judging the word by its sound

parts.note: specs is informal for spectacles

explanation.surface: There are tiny smudges on someone's spectacles.
explanation.definitionFit: Specks are tiny spots or marks.

clue.text: Germanic settler's position

definitions.meaning: a member of a Germanic tribe from Schleswig that settled in eastern England in the 5th century
a standpoint or point of view, a slant taken on a story

explanation.definitionFit: An Angle is one of the Germanic tribe settling Britain; angle also means a viewpoint or stance.

clue.text: Overbearing monarch in ungodly environment

indicators.note: environment means one piece surrounds the other, here the ungodly word round the monarch

parts.note: impious means lacking reverence for God
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A domineering king lives among godless surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperious means arrogantly domineering, expecting to be obeyed.

clue.text: Composition, and so on, written up in books

indicators.note: in means the reversed abbreviation goes inside the books abbreviation

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

indicators.note: written up means in a down entry the letters are set upwards, reading backwards

parts.note: etc. is short for et cetera, and so on

explanation.surface: A musical piece and similar works are reviewed in print.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a musical composition for eight players.

clue.text: Inspect rectory haunted by this?

indicators.note: the run of words is haunted by, holding within it, the thing sought

explanation.surface: An investigator asks what ghost might be stalking the vicarage.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across the join of 'inSPECT REctory', and a rectory might well be haunted by a ghost.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectre is a ghost, the sort of thing said to haunt an old rectory.

clue.text: Lieutenant's turn during tedious task to make us laugh

indicators.note: during means one piece occurs within the other, so it goes inside the task

parts.note: a chore is a tedious task

indicators.note: turn means the letters for the officer are flipped back to front

parts.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: An officer's comic routine in the middle of dull work gets everyone giggling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' looks like a comic act on stage, but it signals that the officer's abbreviation is reversed before going inside the task.
explanation.definitionFit: To chortle is to laugh gleefully, a word coined by Lewis Carroll.

clue.text: A small number in church go across the water

indicators.note: in means the two pieces sit inside the abbreviation for church

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England
no. is the short form of number, so a small number is NO

explanation.surface: A few people in church set off over the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: To canoe is to paddle a light boat across water.

clue.text: Analyse water flowing in Hampshire

definitions.meaning: to examine or try something out
a famous trout river in Hampshire, a county in southern England

explanation.definitionFit: To test is to examine or analyse; the Test is a chalk stream river through Hampshire.

clue.text: Mount found in Estonia, oddly enough

indicators.note: oddly enough means take the letters in odd-numbered places, the first, third, fifth and seventh

explanation.surface: A mountain is unexpectedly discovered in the Baltic state of Estonia.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is a volcano in Sicily, so a mountain.
